messages:
maria: Ran the nightly perf sweep against SM86 FLEET. Noticed ~20% p99 regression on seq≈256 workloads compared to last week. Attaching short profile dump.

maria: ```
PROFILE SUMMARY
model: galactica-7b
seqlen: 256
batch: 1
selected_kernel: bf16_tc_fastpath
latency_p50: 28.3ms
latency_p99: 142.7ms
kv_cache_bytes: 1.15GB
kv_evictions: 19
notes: sudden kv_eviction spikes around token 120-140
```

jonathan: Can you paste the kernel selection table from the autotune run? Curious whether the selection cost accounts for KV memory. @sophie any ideas? :thinking_face:

maria: selection table (trimmed):
```
kernel,batch_throughput,est_latency,est_mem,kernel_score
bf16_tc_fastpath,1200tokens/s,30ms,0.9GB,0.85
fp16_tiled,950tokens/s,40ms,0.4GB,0.78
int8_qsv,600tokens/s,60ms,0.2GB,0.66
```
We ended up picking bf16_tc_fastpath because raw throughput/latency score favored it. But runtime kv_cache growth pushes memory beyond expected and causes evictions -> p99 spikes.

sophie: Sounds like autotune score isn't penalizing per-request KV footprint. We optimize for throughput but KV cache multiplies with seq and can flip the bottleneck. Suggest adding a kv_memory_penalty term into kernel_score.

jonathan: Repro steps? I want to run locally against an SM86 dev box.

maria: repro: `./perf/run --model galactica-7b --seqlen 256 --batch 1 --autotune --arch sm86 --profile-short`
Output snippet: `kernel=bf16_tc_fastpath latency=35ms p99=150ms kv_cache=1.2GB evictions=23`

sophie: Interesting that on SM75 we've historically gone to fp16_tiled for these mid-lengths and didn't see evictions. So the arch detection and tensorcore capability logic is working — it's the scoring.

jonathan: Could it be driver-side workspace allocation differences? Or a different allocation policy on our SM86 builds? Check cuMemPool and driver 545 vs 537. Any recent driver rollouts?

maria: Nodes are on driver 545.2. We rolled that last week (ops note). But the pattern is consistent across nodes with same driver. I think it's score/heuristics.

sophie: Proposal: during the hw-scan/autotune phase run a micro-probe that estimates KV bytes per token for each model and tokenization mode. Add kv_est to kernel table and compute kernel_score = est_latency + alpha*kv_est_bytes_normalized. Tune alpha in canary.

jonathan: +1. Also add a fallback gate: if kv_est + peak_allocation > device_mem * 0.9 then prefer lower-kv kernel even if raw latency is worse. That would avoid evictions.

ci-bot: nightly-regression: 2723456710 report uploaded -> https://ci.internal/reports/2723456710 (contains full flamegraphs and kernel picks) :robot_face:

maria: I'll prototype a quick patch: runtime.autotune.kv_penalty = 0.8 (config flag) and a hard gate threshold runtime.autotune.max_mem_fraction = 0.9. Will run canary on dedicated pool and collect kernels.kv_evictions metric.

sophie: Also add a device capability check that doesn't conflate "tensorcore available" with "fp8 support". Some vendors advertise tensor cores but fp8 math paths are limited. Split flags: device.supportsTensorCore, device.supportsBF16TensorCore, device.supportsFP8.

jonathan: Good call. We saw earlier mismatch where kernel router picked an FP8 path on a device that didn't actually have fp8 dtype support -> fallback at runtime which cost us. Detect early.

maria: Plan: (1) small heuristic change + flag behind opt-in; (2) canary run against 50 nodes sm86 and 50 nodes sm75; (3) dashboards: kernels.kv_evictions, kernels.fallback_count, perf.p99_by_seq; (4) rollback if canary p95/p99 worsens > 5%. ETA: patch by EOD, canary tomorrow morning.

jonathan: Add unit test that simulates KV growth (kv-blaster) and asserts selection prefers lower-kv kernel when gate triggers.

sophie: I'll draft the device capability split and update arch-scan probe to emit supportsFP8 boolean. Small PR from me today.

maria: sweet. tagging this thread for follow-up. will post canary results here. :thumbsup:
